rationale: A written type argument is EVIDENCE. `for (final e in xs)` writes no type for `e`, so before this change `e.load()` published a bare leaf with receiverTypeUnknown even when `xs` was declared `List<Repo>` in the same signature — the element type is written in the source, one type argument away. The analyzer now records the element type of the container types it can read (List/Iterable/Set/Queue/Stream/Iterator/…) from the parameter's or local's own `type_arguments` child, and an UNTYPED for-in over such a variable types its loop variable for the body (receiver evidence class `annotation`: the type was WRITTEN). The inference is deliberately narrow: only a container whose element type is written, and only when the loop variable has no written type of its own. THE BOUNDARY is `dynamic`: it is the absence of a type, not a declaration, and must never become metadata.owner (the resolver would look up a class-like declaration named `dynamic` and fail) — measured before this fixture, a `dynamic d` parameter did exactly that.

expectRelationships.note: THE INFERENCE, through `List<Repo> xs`: the untyped loop variable `r` is typed from the written type argument, so the call target is spelled and the owner channel states the type. Before the fix this row was `calls -> load` with receiverTypeUnknown.
the READ arm on the inferred element type — both arms must see it.

the CONTAINER's own receiver (`xs.length`): the written type is the base `List`. `List` is declared outside this file, so no kind is known here and the owner is allowed — the external-owner case the channel exists for.
THE TYPED FORM still works through the existing collector (`for (final Repo r in ys)`) — the inference branch only fills types that are not already there.
MAP VALUES: `for (final r in byId.values)` over `Map<String, Repo> byId` types `r` from the SECOND written type argument (the value). Before this, `r.load()` was a bare leaf with receiverTypeUnknown.

FUTURE AWAIT: `final repo = await pending;` over `Future<Repo> pending` types `repo` from the written type argument; `repo.load()` is spelled and owned. (calls, not uses: the selector takes an argument list.)
MAP KEYS: `for (final k in byId.keys)` over `Map<String, Repo>` types `k` from the FIRST written type argument; `k.length` is spelled `String.length`.

forbidRelationships.note: THE PRE-FIX BARE LEAF — gone once the written element type is used.
the same pre-fix shape on the read arm.
NO INFERENCE WHERE NOTHING IS WRITTEN — `dynamic xs` writes no element type, so no owner may be guessed. (The row keeps its bare leaf + receiverTypeUnknown cut.)
and definitely not `dynamic` — the absence of a type is not a class-like owner.
THE BOUNDARY CASE: a `dynamic` parameter must never become an owner. Measured before this fix: `d.foo` emitted exactly this row.
THE VALUE'S NAME IS NOT THE OWNER — `Repo` is the type; `xs` is the container's name.
THE PRE-FIX BARE LEAF for the map-values loop (no receiver type).
THE PRE-FIX BARE LEAF for the awaited local (no receiver type).
THE PRE-FIX BARE LEAF for the map-keys loop (no receiver type; it was even mis-owned as Repo before the selector was read).
